brief.topic: The Average Hidden in a Walk to the Pond

s01: A walk to the pond and back has two equal distances.
You stroll out slowly, then return twice as fast.
The faster half does not simply cancel the slower half.
Let the pond be three kilometres away.
At three kilometres an hour, the outward walk takes one hour.
At six kilometres an hour, the return takes half an hour.
The slow part occupies more of your time.
Lay those times beside each other.
Six kilometres have taken one and a half hours.
The average speed is four kilometres an hour.
The simple average of three and six would be four and a half.
That would weight the two speeds equally, though their times are unequal.
For equal distances, time is distance divided by speed.
Add the two times before dividing the whole journey by them.
This gives the harmonic mean of the two speeds.
Its shape remembers that slow travel lasts longer.
If you spent equal times at each speed instead, the ordinary average would work.
The important question is what has been kept equal.
Distance, or time.
A small change in the question changes what an average should mean.

scenes.narration:
A walk to the pond and back has two equal distances. You stroll out slowly, then return twice as fast. The faster half does not simply cancel the slower half.

Let the pond be three kilometres away. At three kilometres an hour, the outward walk takes one hour. At six kilometres an hour, the return takes half an hour. The slow part occupies more of your time.

Lay those times beside each other. Six kilometres have taken one and a half hours. The average speed is four kilometres an hour. The simple average of three and six would be four and a half. That would weight the two speeds equally, though their times are unequal.

For equal distances, time is distance divided by speed. Add the two times before dividing the whole journey by them. This gives the harmonic mean of the two speeds. Its shape remembers that slow travel lasts longer.

If you spent equal times at each speed instead, the ordinary average would work. The important question is what has been kept equal. Distance, or time. A small change in the question changes what an average should mean.
